title: Closed lifted-test criterion and coherence for derived exchange
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and on every small pro-etale site put $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use internal module objects, exact module inverse images and ordinary unbounded total right derived direct images computed on K-injectives [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], in compatible small-site and coefficient universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $s:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\hookrightarrow U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a closed immersion of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $v$ for the specified closed-site lift on affine ind-etale bases [def-exc-closed-site-lift, def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Let $\mathscr T_s$ consist of all affine ind-etale objects $V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C\to Z$ such that both $V$ and $W=v(V)=\operatorname{Spec}C$ are w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal].

Every affine ind-etale object of $Z$ admits a covering by objects of $\mathscr T_s$. For each such $V$, the specified quotient identifies $C/IC=\overline C$ and $W\times_U Z=V$, and $(C,IC)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Evaluation at these $V$ is exact on module sheaves. The functors $R\Gamma(V,-):D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_Z})\to D(\mathbf{Ab})$, for $V\in\mathscr T_s$, jointly detect isomorphisms.

Let $f:X\to U$ be any morphism with $X$ affine, $X_Z=X\times_UZ$, and projections $h:X_Z\to X$ and $f_Z:X_Z\to Z$. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$ be bounded below. For $V\in\mathscr T_s$ put $T=X\times_Uv(V)$ and $T_0=X\times_U V$, with $a:T_0\hookrightarrow T$. If every canonical unit-induced restriction
$$R\Gamma(T,K|_T)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T_0,a^*(K|_T))$$
is an isomorphism, then the specified exchange
$$\beta_{f,s,K}:s^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow R(f_Z)_*h^*K$$
is an isomorphism. The specified exchange is the adjunct of $f_Z^*s^*Rf_*K\cong h^*f^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{h^*\varepsilon}h^*K$, with canonical coefficient and composition comparisons.

These canonical exchanges are natural in $K$, in isomorphisms of the cartesian square, and under pro-etale base change of $U$. The same equations hold on the entire objects $U[Q]\to U$ for arbitrary profinite $Q$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] and after further such parametrization. For any condensed ring map $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ and actual degree-zero module map $M\to\operatorname{Res}N$, the exchanges for $M[0]$ and $N[0]$ commute after scalar restriction with the derived maps induced by that map. The direct-image comparisons are the canonical right-derived ones induced by $f_*\operatorname{Res}=\operatorname{Res}f_*$, without an invertibility assertion. In particular the ordinary scalar-extension unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ has this compatibility. No integrality or lisseness of $f$ or $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: For any affine ind-etale object $V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C$ of $Z$, the specified lift is $v(V)=\operatorname{Spec}H_A(\overline C)$. The closed-site functor theorem identifies its closed fibre with $V$, and the reduction theorem identifies the specified algebra map $C/IC\to\overline C$ as an isomorphism. The henselian-lift theorem applies to this very colimit algebra, so $(C,IC)$ is henselian. Consequently the w-contractibility equivalence for henselian quotients says that $V$ is w-contractible if and only if $v(V)$ is. This uses no finite generation of $I$.

source.place: Tag 09BK (lemma-closed-immersion-affines), Tag 097P (lemma-lift-ind-etale); HRS Corollary 4.4(2) and Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 6.1.1–6.1.2

proof.text: Let $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}B\to Z$ be an affine ind-etale object. Choose a faithfully flat ind-etale $B$-algebra $D$ that is w-contractible. Composition of ind-etale maps makes $\operatorname{Spec}D\to Z$ another affine ind-etale object, and faithful flatness makes $\operatorname{Spec}D\to V_0$ a pro-etale cover. Step 1 makes its specified closed lift w-contractible as well. Thus this cover belongs to $\mathscr T_s$. Since the affine ind-etale basis covers the full site, every site object is covered by tests from $\mathscr T_s$.

proof.text: Use the equivalence between internal modules and section-ring module sheaves, identical on underlying sheaves, sections and restriction maps. Exact evaluation at any w-contractible affine $V$ then applies to the internal modules here. For every unbounded complex $L$, the derived-section theorem identifies $R\Gamma(V,L)$ with its termwise section complex. Exactness gives $H^q(R\Gamma(V,L))=\Gamma(V,\mathcal H^qL)$: apply evaluation to the kernel defining cycles and the cokernel of boundaries. If all these derived sections vanish, each $\mathcal H^qL$ vanishes on all tests. For a section over any site object, restrict to a covering by tests from step 2; all restrictions are zero, so separatedness in the sheaf axiom makes the section zero. Thus every $\mathcal H^qL=0$. The map from the zero complex to a representative of $L$ is a quasi-isomorphism, hence $L=0$ in the derived localization. For a morphism $b$, apply this argument to its cone: evaluation is triangulated by exact-functor descent, so invertibility of every $R\Gamma(V,b)$ makes the evaluated cones zero, and hence the cone of $b$ zero. The distinguished-cone criterion makes $b$ invertible. This proves joint detection for unbounded objects without any convergence assertion.

source.place: Tag 098H (lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible), exact evaluation and derived localization; HRS Lemma 4.1(1), agent cone-and-sheaf-axiom argument

proof.text: For the given affine $f$ and bounded-below $K$, apply the closed-test derived exchange model at each $V\in\mathscr T_s$. Its hypotheses are precisely affineness, bounded-below $K$, and w-contractibility of $V$ and $v(V)$, supplied above. Its two derived isomorphisms identify $R\Gamma(V,\beta_{f,s,K})$ with the specified unit-induced restriction from $T$ to $T_0$. The hypothesis of the item therefore makes every evaluated exchange invertible. Step 3 makes $\beta_{f,s,K}$ invertible. The model explicitly uses the counit-adjunct exchange in the statement, so this proves invertibility of that arrow.

proof.text:
Write $\theta:f_Z^*s^*\cong h^*f^*$ for the canonical pullback comparison. By the square-exchange definition, the transpose of $\beta_K$ is $e_K=h^*\varepsilon_K\circ\theta_{Rf_*K}$. For $t:K\to L$, naturality of $\theta$ and $\varepsilon$ gives
$$h^*t\circ e_K=e_L\circ f_Z^*s^*Rf_*(t).$$
The adjunction bijection makes this the naturality equation for $\beta$. An isomorphism of cartesian squares identifies the two composites of inverse images and hence their $\theta$; conjugate the displayed transpose by those identifications. The counit is transported to the counit, so the same equation proves square-isomorphism naturality. For restriction to any pro-etale object of $U$, use derived slice localization, whose comparisons explicitly preserve units and counits. After those comparisons the restricted transpose is again $h'^*\varepsilon'\circ\theta'$, hence its adjunct is the exchange for the restricted square. Composition comparisons here have the specified adjunction normalization; no arbitrary adjunction on an isomorphic functor is substituted.

source.place: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change): transpose formula; Tag 0D6F and canonical slice comparisons

proof.text: For a condensed ring map, denote scalar restriction on each corner by $r$, the coefficient pullback identification by $p_u:u_R^*r\cong r u_S^*$, and the canonical direct comparison by $d_u:rRu_{*,S}\to Ru_{*,R}r$. At the underived level restriction is the identity on underlying sheaves and maps, and $u_*r=ru_*$ sectionwise. Since the ordinary adjunction Hom bijection on an actual section is unchanged after forgetting scalars, this identity is the ordinary mate of the underived $p_u$. Applying the right-derived comparison unit to this identity constructs $d_u$; since that unit is invertible on K-injective complexes and every object has a K-injective model, this formula determines $d_u$ uniquely. The module categories are Grothendieck abelian by the small-site ring-module Grothendieck theorem and the internal/section-module equivalence, so they have functorial K-injective resolutions. Apply the exact unbounded derived-mate theorem with $L,L'$ the two exact module inverse images, $R,R'$ the two direct images, $G,H$ the two exact scalar restrictions, $\sigma=p_u$, and $\theta=D(p_u)$, which is normalized by $p_u$ on every complex model because all four functors act termwise. Its formula says that the mate of $D(p_u)$ for the unbounded derived adjunctions, precomposed with $r$ of the right-derived unit, is the localized ordinary mate (the identity) followed by the right-derived unit. By the uniqueness just noted this mate is $d_u$, so the counit equation holds:$$r\varepsilon_{u,S}=\varepsilon_{u,R}\circ u_R^*(d_u)\circ p_u^{-1}.$$It holds on all unbounded objects. No preservation of K-injectives by $r$ and no inverse to $d_u$ is used. The closed-test model independently records this comparison and its compatibility with actual coefficient maps.

source.place: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7; existing exact unbounded derived-mate theorem for exact scalar restriction, and the coefficient paragraph of the closed-test model

proof.text:
For an actual map $t:M\to r_XN$, first prove the coefficient equation at $N[0]$ and then compose with $Rf_{*,R}(t)$. Suppressing only the canonical $p$'s, the equation at $N[0]$ is
$$d_{f_Z}\circ r_Z(\beta_S)=\beta_R\circ s_R^*(d_f).$$
Take both transposes under $f_{Z,R}^*\dashv R(f_Z)_{*,R}$. On the left, substitute the counit equation of step 6 for $u=f_Z$ and the transpose $h_S^*\varepsilon_{f,S}\circ\theta_S$; this gives $h_R^*(r_X\varepsilon_{f,S})\circ\theta_S$ with the $p$ identifications. On the right the transpose is $h_R^*\varepsilon_{f,R}\circ\theta_R\circ f_{Z,R}^*s_R^*(d_f)$. Naturality of $\theta$ moves $d_f$ across it; substitute step 6 for $u=f$. Both expressions become the same composite. The pullback $p$'s commute with $\theta$ because all act by the same coefficient-ring action and the same pullback composition on underlying sheaves. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the equation. Naturality from step 5 now gives the asserted square for $t$. The ordinary extension unit is the actual map $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, so it is a special case, with no flatness assumption on scalar extension.

source.place: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7: agent transpose calculation with the noninvertible derived coefficient comparison

proof.text: Finally $U[Q]\to U$ is an entire pro-etale test object for every profinite $Q$, by the profinite-test-object definition; no choice of a point of $Q$ enters. Apply the slice-localization conclusion of step 5 to this object. Applying it again to a further parametrization gives the same equations, since the composition comparisons preserve the composite adjunctions. The coefficient equation of step 7 also restricts along these functors, so it holds on the entire parameter objects and their further parametrizations. None of the arguments of steps 4–7 uses integrality of $f$ or lisseness of $K$.
